sentences.en: This episode of The Rest is History on treason in modern Britain is sponsored by the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 本期关于现代英国叛国罪的《历史的余味》节目由英国国家档案馆赞助播出。

sentences.en: Enjoy the show.
sentences.zh: 祝您收听愉快。

sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《历史的余味》。

sentences.en: And Tom, we are here again at the National Archives for their amazing exhibition, Treason, People,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们再次来到国家档案馆，参观他们精彩的展览《叛国：人民、

sentences.en: Power and Plot.
sentences.zh: 权力与阴谋》。

sentences.en: And last time, we were talking about the Tudors and the medieval period.
sentences.zh: 上次我们讨论了都铎王朝和中世纪时期。

sentences.en: And this time we've reached a real favourite of yours.
sentences.zh: 而这次我们触及了你非常喜欢的一个话题。

sentences.en: You love the sort of 17th, 18th centuries, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你很喜欢 17、18 世纪，对吧？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to be kicking off with a subject that has already provided us with two episodes, namely the trial of Charles I.
sentences.zh: 我想我们将从一个已经为我们提供了两期节目的主题开始，即查理一世的审判。

sentences.en: But we are actually looking at some of the documents that relate to that.
sentences.zh: 但我们实际上是在看一些与此相关的文献。

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's an amazing privilege actually to see these genuine, you know, the stuff of history without resorting completely into cliches.
sentences.zh: 能亲眼看到这些真实的文献，也就是历史的实物，而不完全陷入陈词滥调，这真是一种莫大的荣幸。

sentences.en: And this time we're joined by Neil Johnston, who is absolutely top brain behind this exhibition, the head of the early modern archives here, I think.
sentences.zh: 这次加入我们的是尼尔·约翰斯顿，他是这次展览背后的顶级大脑，我想他也是这里早期现代档案馆的负责人。

sentences.en: And Neil, sort of a dream of yours to see all this stuff out on public consumption?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，能把这些东西公之于众，算是你的梦想吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it's really wonderful to be able to put so many aspects of the collection together.
sentences.zh: 哦，能把收藏的这么多方面整合在一起，真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Because archives are, you know, they're sort of abstract notions for people.
sentences.zh: 因为对人们来说，档案馆往往是某种抽象的概念。

sentences.en: What are they?
sentences.zh: 它们到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, they're collections of records.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们是记录的集合。

sentences.en: And how do you try to explain it to people?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么试着向人们解释的呢？

sentences.en: And this collection is really, really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这个收藏真的非常、非常了不起。

sentences.en: You know, where I'm from, the equivalent collection was blown up a hundred years ago.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在我家乡，同类的收藏在一百年前就被炸毁了。

sentences.en: So this to me is really, really special, being able to go back to the 1352 Act, the Treason Act, as it is, and even before that, as you can see in the exhibition,
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，能够追溯到 1352 年的《叛国法案》，正如展览中所见，甚至在此之前，

sentences.en: and then bring it all the way forward to the modern day.
sentences.zh: 然后一直延续到现代，这真的非常特别。

sentences.en: So the collection here in Britain is really, really special.
sentences.zh: 所以英国的这个收藏确实非常、非常特别。

sentences.en: It's remarkable.
sentences.zh: 这太了不起了。

sentences.en: Well, Neil, we, just before we recorded this, you showed us the record of parliamentary proceedings written in late 1649, 1650, detailing the events of the trial of Charles I.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，在我们录制之前，你向我们展示了 1649 年末至 1650 年编写的议会记录，详细记载了查理一世审判的经过。

sentences.en: And it's in a kind of little brown book.
sentences.zh: 它装在一本棕色的小书里。

sentences.en: And on the cover, it's got the trial of the king, just in case anyone has any doubted to it.
sentences.zh: 封面上写着“国王的审判”，以防有人对此有任何怀疑。

sentences.en: I mean, it is incredible to see the physical documents that relate to this subject that Dominic, you and I, you know, we did these two episodes on, absolutely up closed.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，能近距离看到多米尼克你和我做过两期节目的那个主题的相关实物文献，真是不可思议。

sentences.en: I mean, how does it make you feel when you look at, you know, it has the column of the people who are sitting in judgment on the king.
sentences.zh: 当你看到上面列着那些审判国王的人的名字时，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: I mean, how does it make you feel to see those names written down in ink on paper?
sentences.zh: 看着那些用墨水写在纸上的名字，你有什么感觉？

sentences.en: Well, if you think of the importance of that event, in terms of legal history, in terms of
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你考虑到那件事在法律史和

sentences.en: political history, going and executing a monarch is an extremely rare event in any circumstances.
sentences.zh: 政治史上的重要性，处决一位君主在任何情况下都是极其罕见的事件。

sentences.en: So I wouldn't say, I wouldn't go so far to say it's quite moving, but, you know, it's, you can feel the importance of the event nearly coming off the page.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会说这很感人，但你能感觉到那件事的重要性几乎要从纸面上溢出来。

sentences.en: You can see, like the journal is very, very detailed.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到，这本日志非常、非常详细。

sentences.en: It was written by the clerks who were there during, on each day during the trial of the king in the, in early 1649.
sentences.zh: 它是 1649 年初国王审判期间，在场的书记员每天记录的。

sentences.en: You can nearly feel the stress coming off the pages as the court constitutes itself from the rump of the House of Commons and it
sentences.zh: 当法庭从下议院的残余议员中组成，并

sentences.en: authorises and empowers itself to put the king on trial for treason.
sentences.zh: 授权自己以叛国罪审判国王时，你几乎能感受到纸页间透出的压力。

sentences.en: So could we look at it specifically in the context of treason, the act of treason that we
sentences.zh: 那么，我们能否具体在叛国罪的背景下审视它？即我们在

sentences.en: began the previous episode with, 1351, 52, depending where you're coming from, it, the definition of treason is plotting against the king.
sentences.zh: 上一集开头提到的 1351 年或 1352 年的叛国罪定义，叛国罪的定义就是密谋反对国王。

sentences.en: You know, not just compassing the death of the king, but imagining the death of the king.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不仅仅是图谋国王的死亡，而是构想国王的死亡。

sentences.en: 1649, they're putting the king on trial.
sentences.zh: 1649 年，他们正在审判国王。

sentences.en: So presumably Edward III's act is, is hopeless for that because it brands them as traitors.
sentences.zh: 那么想必爱德华三世的法案对他们来说是没用的，因为它把他们打成了叛徒。

sentences.en: Well, it depends on how you view sovereignty and the Commons claims sovereignty.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你如何看待主权，而下议院声称拥有主权。

sentences.en: It also has de facto authority because it's won the two civil wars.
sentences.zh: 因为它赢得了两次内战，所以它也拥有事实上的权威。

sentences.en: So it reverses the previous understanding of what treason is.
sentences.zh: 所以它颠覆了之前对叛国罪的理解。

sentences.en: Legally, yes, they are acting.
sentences.zh: 从法律上讲，是的，他们的行为是……

sentences.en: It's extrajudicial, let's say.
sentences.zh: 我们称之为法外行为。

sentences.en: What they've done is illegal.
sentences.zh: 他们的所作所为是非法的。

sentences.en: Charles doesn't recognise the court, does he?
sentences.zh: 查理不承认这个法庭，对吧？

sentences.en: The king refuses to recognise the authority of the courts to put him on trial and he won't plead.
sentences.zh: 国王拒绝承认法庭审判他的权威，他拒绝认罪。

sentences.en: And you can see that the court solicitors, John Cook, is almost barracking him to enter a plea because a case cannot initiate.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到法庭律师约翰·库克几乎是在逼迫他认罪，因为案件无法启动。

sentences.en: So the court is very, very careful to follow the procedures that would ordinarily have been followed, say for a treason trial or a murder trial.
sentences.zh: 所以法庭非常、非常小心地遵循通常用于叛国罪或谋杀罪审判的程序。

sentences.en: They are very, very clear on the proceedings, but the king won't enter a plea.
sentences.zh: 他们对程序非常、非常清楚，但国王就是不认罪。

sentences.en: So the case shouldn't actually continue, but they, they ignore this.
sentences.zh: 所以案件本不该继续，但他们忽略了这一点。

sentences.en: But what, what law would they, I mean, what law can they bring?
sentences.zh: 但是他们能引用什么法律呢？

sentences.en: There is no law to bring.
sentences.zh: 没有法律可引用。

sentences.en: So, uh, they, they claim authority.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们声称拥有权威。

sentences.en: They claim that under the treason act, the king, by raising his banners, he levied war on the people and the commons
sentences.zh: 他们声称根据《叛国法案》，国王通过竖起旗帜，向人民发动了战争，而下议院

sentences.en: claimed that it was sovereign within the people and the king had lost the right to claim this.
sentences.zh: 声称主权在民，国王已经失去了主张这一点的权利。

sentences.en: So the pages you've chosen for us, is that what they're arguing, basically?
sentences.zh: 所以你为我们挑选的这些页面，基本上就是在争论这些吗？

sentences.en: So this is, you can see Cook and the king arguing back and forth, the king refusing to accept
sentences.zh: 你可以看到库克和国王在来回争论，国王拒绝承认

sentences.en: that he had levied war, that he had committed treason and Cook demanding, absolutely demanding that he entered a plea.
sentences.zh: 他发动了战争，犯下了叛国罪，而库克要求，绝对要求他认罪。

sentences.en: Are they framing the idea of, of treason in a biblical context, a Roman context, an Anglo-Saxon context?
sentences.zh: 他们是在圣经、罗马或盎格鲁-撒克逊的背景下构建叛国罪的概念吗？

sentences.en: I mean, where are they getting the idea that there is a case for the king to answer from?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们是从哪里得出国王有罪需要答辩这一想法的？

sentences.en: What's the legal underpinning for that case?
sentences.zh: 该案的法律依据是什么？

sentences.en: The 1352 act, the idea of levying war against the king is what, is really what they're, against the people is what they're saying.
sentences.zh: 1352 年的法案，即发动反对国王的战争，实际上他们说的是反对人民。

sentences.en: And, but they're, what they've tried to do is they've tried to perform this, uh, sort of jump to move, to shift the center of authority from
sentences.zh: 他们试图做的是进行这种跳跃式的举动，将权威中心从

sentences.en: the crown, from the person of the king to the state.
sentences.zh: 王室、从国王个人转移到国家。

sentences.en: And that they say, as the commons of England, they are the true representatives of the people, not the monarch.
sentences.zh: 他们说，作为英格兰的下议院，他们是人民的真正代表，而不是君主。

sentences.en: And this is how they go forward and create a republic.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们前进并建立共和国的方式。

sentences.en: And that they say that they, it is the commons that is sovereign, not the king.
sentences.zh: 他们说下议院才是主权所在，而不是国王。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not going to say it's not true because they have the authority to do, they have defeated the royalist forces.
sentences.zh: 现在，我不会说这不是真的，因为他们有权这样做，他们击败了保皇党军队。

sentences.en: And so it's really about power and treason is theater.
sentences.zh: 所以这实际上是关于权力的，而叛国罪是一场戏。

sentences.en: Treason trials are generally theater trials.
sentences.zh: 叛国罪审判通常都是表演性的审判。

sentences.en: So, uh, some, like in the early modern period, the, the, the verdict is almost a foregone conclusion.
sentences.zh: 所以，在早期现代，判决几乎是预先注定的。

sentences.en: So this wasn't, this was different.
sentences.zh: 但这不一样。

sentences.en: This was so unprecedented.
sentences.zh: 这是史无前例的。

sentences.en: It's, it's not that they were making it up as they were going along, but they were adapting throughout the trial.
sentences.zh: 并不是说他们边走边编，但他们在审判过程中一直在调整。

sentences.en: But I suppose the, um, in a way they are, they are the representative of the future because
sentences.zh: 但我认为，在某种程度上，他们是未来的代表，因为

sentences.en: the idea that, um, treason can be acted against an entire people, against the nation is the future, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 叛国罪可以针对全体人民、针对国家这一理念是未来的方向，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, that is the understanding probably that most people have of it now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能是现在大多数人对它的理解。

sentences.en: It's not specifically directed against the monarch.
sentences.zh: 它不再专门针对君主。

sentences.en: It's not against the person of the monarch necessarily anymore.
sentences.zh: 它不一定再针对君主个人了。

sentences.en: And what we see here now is this shift into a more, both a more modern understanding of treason and also the beginning
sentences.zh: 我们现在看到的是向更现代的叛国罪理解的转变，同时也开始了

sentences.en: of the redundancy of the treason act as it was framed in 1352.
sentences.zh: 1352 年制定的《叛国法案》的冗余化。

sentences.en: So they have to adapt and the commons or the rump of the long parliament as it was who prosecuted the king, they weren't
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须适应，而下议院，或者说审判国王的残余议会，他们并不是

sentences.en: the first or the last power we can say, or government, if we want to call them a government, to adapt the treason laws to their own circumstances.
sentences.zh: 第一个也不是最后一个将叛国法适应于自身情况的政权，如果我们称他们为政府的话。

sentences.en: So just on the document.
sentences.zh: 关于这份文件。

sentences.en: So when people come to the exhibition, what they're actually seeing is something written, not on the day, but afterwards from, from reports.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们来到展览时，他们看到的实际上是事后根据报告编写的东西，而不是当天写的。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: There you write up the reports afterwards.
sentences.zh: 是的，事后整理报告。

sentences.en: So the clerks within the commons will have been taken notes, uh, contemporary notes as events happened, and then they will have written them up afterwards.
sentences.zh: 下议院的书记员会在事件发生时做笔记，即当下的记录，然后事后整理出来。

sentences.en: They were instructed by the house of commons to do this in February, 1649.
sentences.zh: 1649 年 2 月，下议院指示他们这样做。

sentences.en: And it took about a year for that volume to emerge.
sentences.zh: 那卷书花了大约一年时间才问世。

sentences.en: There's two or three volumes and they were, they're heavily disputed, but they are keenly important and they become even more important.
sentences.zh: 有两三卷，它们备受争议，但它们非常重要，而且变得越来越重要。

sentences.en: Well, I was about to say, so fast forward to 1658, 59, 60, when you've got so much turbulence, all the other alternatives exhaust themselves.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，快进到 1658、59、60 年，当时局势动荡不安，所有其他选择都耗尽了。

sentences.en: So suddenly it becomes obvious that Charles II is, is basically the only alternative left.
sentences.zh: 所以突然间显而易见，查理二世基本上是剩下的唯一选择。

sentences.en: Is there no discussion about destroying these documents, which actually are quite incriminating?
sentences.zh: 难道没有关于销毁这些实际上相当有罪证的文件的讨论吗？

sentences.en: The power has shifted, you know, Cromwell dies, Oliver Cromwell dies in September 1658 and his son takes over, but he doesn't have that authority to deal with the huge competing
sentences.zh: 权力已经转移了，你知道，克伦威尔去世了，奥利弗·克伦威尔于 1658 年 9 月去世，他的儿子接手了，但他没有权威来处理军队内部、军队中的清教徒以及议会内部巨大的竞争利益。

sentences.en: interests within the army, the Puritans within the army, within parliament.
sentences.zh: 议会本身不想让军队对平民发号施令。

sentences.en: Parliament itself doesn't want the army dictating to civilians.
sentences.zh: 军队也不想被平民指手画脚。

sentences.en: The army doesn't want to be dictated to by civilians.
sentences.zh: 所以，一种政治无政府状态爆发了。

sentences.en: So, uh, a form of political anarchy breaks out.
sentences.zh: 最终，唯一真正有合法统治权的人是查理·斯图亚特，他在 1660 年非常巧妙地避开了

sentences.en: And eventually the, the last person who has legitimacy really to rule is Charles Stuart, he sidesteps very, very cleverly in 1660,
sentences.zh: 1640 年代导致内战和他父亲被处决的那些争论。

sentences.en: the arguments that had been put forward in the 1640s that caused civil wars and the execution of his father.
sentences.zh: 随着 1660 年 3 月和 4 月新议会的出现，他们无法就接下来发生什么达成一致。

sentences.en: And as a new parliament emerges in 1660, in March and April 1660, they cannot agree in what's to happen.
sentences.zh: 一个意想不到的人几乎终结了共和国，那就是将军

sentences.en: And an unlikely source had almost ended the Republic, which is General
sentences.zh: 乔治·蒙克，他是苏格兰军队的指挥官。

sentences.en: George Monk, who was the commander of the army in Scotland.
sentences.zh: 他在 1660 年 1 月、2 月向伦敦的进军实际上终结了共和国，1660 年 3 月选出了新议会。

sentences.en: His march on London in January,
sentences.zh: 它召开了会议，公约议会于 1660 年 4 月召开。

sentences.en: February 1660 virtually ends the Republic and a new parliament is assembled in March, is voted for in March 1660.
sentences.zh: 蒙克实际上说，任何不支持查理·斯图亚特的人，都保持沉默。

sentences.en: And it meets, the convention parliament meets in April 1660.
sentences.zh: 这给了国王机会，此时查理·斯图亚特已经流亡了 11 年，他成为了查理二世，他派出了

sentences.en: And Monk effectively says, anybody who is not for Charles Stuart, be silent.
sentences.zh: 他的特使约翰·格伦维尔爵士，在 1660 年 5 月 1 日，他提交了所谓的《布雷达宣言》。

sentences.en: And this gives the king, the king had been in exile for 11 years at this point, Charles Stuart, who becomes Charles II, he sends his
sentences.zh: 有了这份文件，国王绕过了所有人。

sentences.en: emissary, Sir John Grenville, um, on the 1st of May, 1660, he hands in what's called his declaration of Brida.
sentences.zh: 这是一项非常、非常聪明的政治举措，他说，我不会重打内战。

sentences.en: And with this document, the king sidesteps everybody.
sentences.zh: 我将让议会负责决定过去十年中易手的土地归属问题。

sentences.en: It's a very, very clever piece of politics where he, he says, I will not refight the civil wars.
sentences.zh: 这是一个他们无法解决的问题。

sentences.en: I'm going to make parliament responsible for deciding who, who wins and loses about land that has exchanged hands over the last decade.
sentences.zh: 他们在爱尔兰试图解决它，结果却完全搞砸了，持续了近三十年。

sentences.en: And that's, it's a question they can't resolve.
sentences.zh: 但第三点，也是最重要的一点，在很多方面，他说，只要不伤害王国，我将允许人们拥有良心自由。

sentences.en: They tried to resolve it in Ireland and it goes completely wrong for, um, almost three decades.
sentences.zh: 所以所有想要遵循英国国教教义的人，他们似乎很高兴。

sentences.en: But thirdly, and most importantly, in many ways, he says, I will allow people to have liberty of conscience once they are not harming the kingdom.
sentences.zh: 清教徒似乎很高兴。

sentences.en: So everybody who wants to conform to the teachings of the
sentences.zh: 浸信会教徒和独立派教徒。

sentences.en: Church of England, they seem to be happy.
sentences.zh: 所以这一招，他算是消除了人们对他回归的恐惧或不满。

sentences.zh: 但它很快就被镇压了。

sentences.en: The French had tried to invade at the end of 1796, but they couldn't land.
sentences.zh: 法国人曾试图在1796年底入侵，但他们无法登陆。

sentences.en: In December 1796, a fleet had been sent from Brest to land at Bantry Bay, but the seas were too high, the storms were too big.
sentences.zh: 1796年12月，一支舰队从布雷斯特出发前往班特里湾登陆，但海浪太大，风暴太强。

sentences.en: So the fleet had to abandon and the British then made every effort to ensure that a fleet couldn't sail directly to Ireland again
sentences.zh: 所以舰队不得不放弃，英国人随后尽了一切努力确保舰队无法再次直接航行到爱尔兰，

sentences.en: without being known about and that, as I say, the United Irishmen had been neutered as a political organization.
sentences.zh: 而不被察觉，正如我所说，联合爱尔兰人作为一个政治组织已经被阉割了。

sentences.en: So could I...
sentences.zh: 所以我可以……

sentences.en: Just on the theme of republicanism, I mean, to argue for a republic is, by definition, I guess, to be hostile to a monarchy and therefore inherently treasonous.
sentences.zh: 就共和主义这个主题而言，我的意思是，主张建立共和国，根据定义，我想就是对君主制怀有敌意，因此本质上是叛国的。

sentences.en: At what point does arguing for a republic cease to be seen as treasonous by the government?
sentences.zh: 政府在什么时候不再认为主张建立共和国是叛国行为？

sentences.en: It doesn't really.
sentences.zh: 其实并没有。

sentences.en: You know, if we look at 1916, the men who fought, men and women who fought in the 1960s to rising in 1916, they're also...
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们看看1916年，那些战斗的人，在1916年起义中战斗的男男女女，他们也……

sentences.en: But I'm not talking just specifically in the Irish context, more generally in the British context.
sentences.zh: 但我不是专门在爱尔兰背景下谈论，而是更广泛地在英国背景下谈论。

sentences.en: But some in the reign of Queen Victoria, there are lots of republicans.
sentences.zh: 但在维多利亚女王统治时期，有很多共和主义者。

sentences.en: There's a lot of republicans.
sentences.zh: 有很多共和主义者。

sentences.en: Presumably anyone who's arguing for a republic in the reign of Queen Victoria, say, is committing treason, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 大概任何在维多利亚女王统治时期主张建立共和国的人，都在犯叛国罪，不是吗？

sentences.en: Under the wording of the Act, yes.
sentences.zh: 根据法案的措辞，是的。

sentences.en: But it's much more difficult to prosecute.
sentences.zh: 但起诉起来要困难得多。

sentences.en: So the crown shows away from it in many ways.
sentences.zh: 所以王室在很多方面都避开了它。

sentences.en: Not entirely, but these ideas are out there now.
sentences.zh: 不完全是，但这些思想现在已经传播开来。

sentences.en: There's so many people...
sentences.zh: 有这么多人……

sentences.en: So there's an acceptance that basically it's not going to...
sentences.zh: 所以人们接受了这一点，基本上它不会……

sentences.en: It's simple practicality that there's so many people believe in the republic now, in republicanism now, that it's simply...
sentences.zh: 这只是简单的实用主义，现在有这么多人相信共和国，相信共和主义，以至于它简直……

sentences.en: There's no way you can prosecute everybody who believes that.
sentences.zh: 你不可能起诉所有相信这一点的人。

sentences.en: To a point, yes.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，是的。

sentences.en: And also, the loyalism in Britain, loyalty to the crown, is also a hugely powerful political force.
sentences.zh: 而且，英国的保皇主义，对王室的忠诚，也是一股巨大的政治力量。

sentences.en: So it's a real dichotomy.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个真正的二分法。

sentences.en: You know, and if we look at the risings that happen, or the attempted risings, and the conspiracies,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我们看看发生的起义，或者未遂起义，以及阴谋，

sentences.en: the Cato Street conspiracy, the Newport Rising, 1848 in France, and then how it spills over into Britain,
sentences.zh: 卡托街阴谋、纽波特起义、1848年的法国，以及它如何蔓延到英国，

sentences.en: these fears of monarchical overthrow, they don't go away, and people are prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 这些对推翻君主制的恐惧并没有消失，人们仍然受到起诉。

sentences.en: But it continues to be propagated by the ideas of the French Revolution, and by Payne, and by Hardian.
sentences.zh: 但它继续受到法国大革命思想、潘恩和哈迪思想的传播。

sentences.en: But there's a general sense that the Act of Treason, although it remains on the statute book, is becoming...
sentences.zh: 但人们普遍认为，《叛国法》虽然仍然保留在法典中，但正在变得……

sentences.en: it's too kind of nebulous a thing to hold legal water.
sentences.zh: 它太模糊了，无法在法律上站得住脚。

sentences.en: And is that why, over the course of the 20th century, even against the backdrop of growing republicanism,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在20世纪，即使在共和主义日益增长的背景下，

sentences.en: of Ireland becoming independent, and so on, that you see the Act of Treason used less and less?
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰独立等等，你看到《叛国法》的使用越来越少了吗？

sentences.en: And I'm right that the very last person to be executed for treason in Britain is William Joyce, better known as Lord Hoar Hoar.
sentences.zh: 我说得对吗，英国最后一个因叛国罪被处决的人是威廉·乔伊斯，也就是众所周知的“霍霍勋爵”。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 那是对的吗？

sentences.en: That's correct, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那是正确的，是的。

sentences.en: So what's the...
sentences.zh: 那么，什么是……

sentences.en: and that is done essentially on a legal technicality, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这本质上是基于法律技术细节完成的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it turns out he's not even a British citizen.
sentences.zh: 因为事实证明他甚至不是英国公民。

sentences.en: So Joyce was born in Brooklyn, but he falsified documents to get a British passport.
sentences.zh: 乔伊斯出生在布鲁克林，但他伪造了文件以获得英国护照。

sentences.en: So this was how the court, in taking out a passport, you are claiming allegiance to the crown.
sentences.zh: 所以法院就是这样认定的，申请护照就意味着你宣誓效忠王室。

sentences.en: And we should just say, for those who don't know about him, that he goes to Nazi Germany, and he broadcasts to Britain from Germany throughout the war.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解他的人，我们应该说，他去了纳粹德国，并在整个战争期间从德国向英国广播。

sentences.en: And so when he's captured after the war, it looks a kind of open and shut case.
sentences.zh: 所以当他在战后被捕时，这看起来是一个证据确凿的案子。

sentences.en: It must have done.
sentences.zh: 肯定是的。

sentences.en: Well, he disputed that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他对此提出了异议。

sentences.en: He said he hadn't committed treason, but of course he had.
sentences.zh: 他说他没有犯叛国罪，但当然他确实犯了。

sentences.en: You know, so it's...
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以它是……

sentences.en: the treason legislation, the 1352 legislation, becomes much, much harder to prosecute people under.
sentences.zh: 叛国法，即1352年的法律，在起诉人们时变得越来越困难了。

sentences.en: There's also the peril for a government of conducting a trial in open court, because it allows people to defend themselves and produce their own evidence under the...
sentences.zh: 政府在公开法庭进行审判也存在风险，因为它允许人们为自己辩护，并根据……出示自己的证据。

sentences.en: Because there are no bills of attainter.
sentences.zh: 因为现在没有剥夺公民权法案了。

sentences.en: I mean, is that simply because they have become illegal?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仅仅是因为它们已经变得不合法了吗？

sentences.en: I mean, no one would dream of bringing an attainder against someone now.
sentences.zh: 我是说，现在没人会想到对某人提出剥夺公民权法案。

sentences.en: I can think of loads of people who are bringing a bill of attainder against you.
sentences.zh: 我能想到很多人会对你提出剥夺公民权法案。

sentences.en: I mean, is the opportunity to do that still on the statute book?
sentences.zh: 我是说，这样做机会还在法典上吗？

sentences.en: Or...
sentences.zh: 或者……

sentences.en: As far as I'm aware, I think the laSt...
sentences.zh: 据我所知，我想最后一次……

sentences.en: You know, people like Churchill during the war, and as the tide of the war was turning during the Second World War,
sentences.zh: 你知道，像丘吉尔这样的人在战争期间，随着第二次世界大战战局的转变，

sentences.en: Churchill, they were trying to deal with the question of, what on earth are we going to do with the Nazi leaders?
sentences.zh: 丘吉尔，他们试图处理这个问题，我们到底该拿纳粹领导人怎么办？

sentences.en: How are we going to deal with these men if we capture them?
sentences.zh: 如果我们抓住了这些人，我们该如何处置他们？

sentences.en: What will we do with Hitler?
sentences.zh: 我们该拿希特勒怎么办？

sentences.en: What court can try Hitler?
sentences.zh: 什么法庭能审判希特勒？

sentences.en: So, initially, it was put to Churchill that, well, we could attaint him.
sentences.zh: 所以，最初有人向丘吉尔建议，嗯，我们可以剥夺他的公民权。

sentences.en: And, of course, he scoffed at it.
sentences.zh: 当然，他对此嗤之以鼻。

sentences.en: He dismissed the idea.
sentences.zh: 他驳回了这个想法。

sentences.en: Could the British Parliament attaint Hitler?
sentences.zh: 英国议会能剥夺希特勒的公民权吗？

sentences.en: Yes, it could.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think in the eyes of the world, that might be lame.
sentences.zh: 我认为在世界眼中，那可能显得很无力。

sentences.en: So, we've got one last document, which I know you picked out for us.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们还有最后一份文件，我知道是你为我们挑选的。

sentences.en: So, we just need to rewind a little bit from Lord Haw-Haw.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们需要从“霍霍勋爵”那里稍微倒带一下。

sentences.en: So, in the First World War, again, from London's perspective, this looks like a real open and shut case of treason.
sentences.zh: 所以，在第一次世界大战中，从伦敦的角度来看，这看起来又是一起真正的证据确凿的叛国案。

sentences.en: But I'm imagining you're going to see it differently, which is why you picked it out.
sentences.zh: 但我猜你会以不同的方式看待它，这就是你选择它的原因。

sentences.en: So, this is the Easter Rising, 1916.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是1916年的复活节起义。

sentences.en: And, obviously, as a Dubliner, you've got a particular stake in this.
sentences.zh: 显然，作为一个都柏林人，你对此有特殊的关切。

sentences.en: I'm also a historian, and I can distance myself on it in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我也是一名历史学家，在某些方面我可以对此保持客观。

sentences.en: But what we have in the collection that we found is the bottom half of the proclamation, the 1916 proclamation that Patrick Pearce read out from the steps of the GPO,
sentences.zh: 但我们在收藏中发现的是宣言的下半部分，即帕特里克·皮尔斯在邮政总局台阶上宣读的1916年宣言，

sentences.en: the General Post Office, on Sackville Street, what's now O'Connell Street in Dublin.
sentences.zh: 也就是都柏林萨克维尔街，即现在的奥康奈尔街上的邮政总局。

sentences.en: And there's a wonderful story about this document in that the type had been confiscated to print the document a few days before the Rising was to break out.
sentences.zh: 关于这份文件有一个精彩的故事，那就是在起义爆发前几天，印刷该文件的铅字被没收了。

sentences.en: So, they had to quickly get another set of type.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们不得不迅速弄到另一套铅字。

sentences.en: But they only had enough to print the top half of the document, and they reamed off how many copies of everything they did.
sentences.zh: 但他们只有足够的铅字来印刷文件的上半部分，而且他们印了好多份。

sentences.en: And then they reset the type and printed the bottom half.
sentences.zh: 然后他们重新排版并印刷了下半部分。

sentences.en: And they left the type in the machine.
sentences.zh: 他们把铅字留在了机器里。

sentences.en: And they ran around the corner, and that was printed in Liberty Hall in Dublin, right on the Liffey, the very tall building now on the Liffey.
sentences.zh: 他们跑到拐角处，那是在都柏林利菲河畔的自由大厅印刷的，就是现在利菲河边那座很高的建筑。

sentences.en: And when the British forces re-secured Dublin a few days later, they go into Liberty Hall and they find the printing press that the 1916 proclamation was produced on.
sentences.zh: 几天后，当英军重新控制都柏林时，他们进入自由大厅，发现了印刷1916年宣言的印刷机。

sentences.en: And they produce several more copies.
sentences.zh: 他们又印了几份。

sentences.en: And that ended up in Sean McDiarmid's court-martial.
sentences.zh: 这最终成了肖恩·麦克迪尔马达军事法庭的证据。

sentences.en: So, martial law is imposed upon Ireland after the Easter Rising breaks out, which is why the rebels, the leaders as they were, are tried by court-martial.
sentences.zh: 所以，复活节起义爆发后，爱尔兰实施了戒严法，这就是为什么叛军，也就是当时的领导人，要接受军事法庭审判的原因。

sentences.en: And they're tried and executed in secret as opposed to giving them an opportunity to air their views in public or their raison d'etre or their reasons for rebelling.
sentences.zh: 他们被秘密审判并处决，而不是让他们有机会在公众面前表达自己的观点，或者陈述他们的存在理由或叛乱原因。

sentences.en: And the papers there you can see in front of you are from the courts-martial that were conducted against the rebel leaders.
sentences.zh: 你面前的那些文件就是针对叛军领导人进行的军事法庭审判记录。

sentences.en: So these are the official records.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是官方记录。

sentences.en: Most certainly, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: And the handwriting.
sentences.zh: 还有笔迹。

sentences.en: So some of them are typed and there's handwriting scribbled on this one that you've got to open at.
sentences.zh: 所以有些是打印的，而你打开的这一份上有潦草的笔迹。

sentences.en: So what's the handwriting all about?
sentences.zh: 那么这些笔迹是关于什么的？

sentences.en: The writing is just, you know, the court-martial gathering evidence as quickly as it can
sentences.zh: 这些文字只是，你知道，军事法庭在尽可能快地收集证据，

sentences.en: and drawing in all the intelligence reports that had been produced in the months and years subsequent,
sentences.zh: 并汇总了随后几个月和几年内产生的所有情报报告，

sentences.en: I mean previous.
sentences.zh: 我是说之前的。

sentences.en: And they're being laid out for the court.
sentences.zh: 它们正被提交给法庭。

sentences.en: So to overwhelmingly prove guilt.
sentences.zh: 为了压倒性地证明有罪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, no one, we wouldn't, I mean, no one normally, no reasonably sane person would think of this as a case of treason now, I suppose, would they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有人，我们不会，我是说，现在没有一个理智的人会认为这是叛国罪，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, this is something that we see certainly with those who had rebelled in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实是我们从那些在爱尔兰叛乱的人身上看到的。

sentences.en: They see themselves as fighting a war.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己是在打仗。

sentences.en: But they weren't loyal to the Crown, so they weren't committing treason.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不效忠于王室，所以他们没有犯叛国罪。

sentences.en: They were seeking independence.
sentences.zh: 他们是在寻求独立。

sentences.en: So, I mean, one case that I do know, I mean, in 1981, the Queen is doing the trooping of colour
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我知道的一个案例，在1981年，女王正在进行皇家军队阅兵仪式，

sentences.en: and a man comes out of the crowd and fires six blank bullets at her.
sentences.zh: 一个人从人群中走出来，向她开了六发空包弹。

sentences.en: And he is charged with treason, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 他被指控犯有叛国罪，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because, and that is presumably because he is directly targeting the figure of the monarch.
sentences.zh: 因为，这大概是因为他直接针对的是君主的形象。

sentences.en: So in a way, we're going back to the medieval understanding that actually treason laws can be applied when the subjects of a monarch are targeting the person of the monarch.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们回到了中世纪的理解，即当君主的臣民针对君主本人时，叛国法实际上是可以适用的。

sentences.en: Intertraction of the 1352 legislation, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对1352年法律的解读，是的。

sentences.en: But otherwise, it's too cumbersome a mechanism to apply.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，它是一个太繁琐的适用机制。

sentences.en: It's nebulous.
sentences.zh: 它很模糊。

sentences.en: It's not guaranteed to return a verdict of guilt.
sentences.zh: 它不能保证能做出有罪判决。

sentences.en: And there is also other legislation that can be used at this point.
sentences.zh: 而且此时还有其他法律可以使用。

sentences.en: So the Crown doesn't...
sentences.zh: 所以王室并不……

sentences.en: Can I ask you a question?
sentences.zh: 我可以问你一个问题吗？

sentences.en: You may not want to answer this question.
sentences.zh: 你可能不想回答这个问题。

sentences.en: But right at the beginning of this, of these two episodes, I read from an article that the government is planning to refine and reframe the treason law.
sentences.zh: 但在这一系列两集节目的最开始，我读到一篇文章说政府计划完善和重构叛国法。

sentences.en: Do you think that the treason law is redeemable, that it can be changed adequately?
sentences.zh: 你认为叛国法还有挽救的余地吗，它能被充分修改吗？

sentences.en: Or is that not a question that you can answer?
sentences.zh: 还是说这不是你能回答的问题？

sentences.en: I wouldn't feel I'm qualified to answer it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我没有资格回答这个问题。

sentences.en: What I can say, it won't be the first time that a government has tried to not amend the original law, but update the terms in which a government makes it useful to them.
sentences.zh: 我能说的是，这不会是政府第一次试图修改原始法律，而是更新政府认为对其有用的条款。

sentences.en: So we see it throughout the century, like this act sitting here right in front of me.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在整个世纪都能看到这一点，就像我面前放着的这份法案一样。

sentences.en: You know, they are...
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们是……

sentences.en: That's the...
sentences.zh: 那是……

sentences.en: The act of indemnity.
sentences.zh: 《赔偿法案》。

sentences.en: Brought to you by Charles II.
sentences.zh: 由查理二世带给你们的。

sentences.en: Yeah, the act of...
sentences.zh: 是的，《赔偿法案》……

sentences.en: There is a law that emerges in 1661, which redefines treason, that says you cannot even seek to harm the person of the king, Charles II.
sentences.zh: 1661年出现了一项法律，重新定义了叛国罪，规定你甚至不能试图伤害国王查理二世本人。

sentences.en: So governments throughout the centuries, really, have tried to do this, update the law to the circumstances of the time.
sentences.zh: 所以几个世纪以来的政府，确实都试图这样做，根据当时的具体情况更新法律。

sentences.en: Neil, this has been absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，这真是太迷人了。

sentences.en: And so many...
sentences.zh: 还有很多……

sentences.en: I mean, Tom, you and I were looking at the documents before we started recording.
sentences.zh: 我是说，汤姆，你和我之前在开始录制前看了这些文件。

sentences.en: And it's an amazing privilege to be able to look at the sort of, you know, the handwriting on the parchment or the paper.
sentences.zh: 能够看到羊皮纸或纸张上的笔迹，这真是一种莫大的荣幸。

sentences.en: And the Popish plot or whatever.
sentences.zh: 还有“教皇阴谋”之类的东西。

sentences.en: Now, when we ended the previous episode, we asked Ewan to identify one person whom he would save,
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们结束上一集时，我们请尤恩选出一个人，他会拯救他，

sentences.en: and one case of treason, which, you know, he would definitely be the hanging judge.
sentences.zh: 以及一个叛国罪案例，你知道，他绝对会成为那个判处死刑的法官。

sentences.en: So it would be remiss of us not to ask you the same question, Neil.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们不问你同样的问题，尼尔，那将是我们的失职。

sentences.en: I can tell you who I'd get rid of.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你我想除掉谁。

sentences.en: Who'd you get rid of?
sentences.zh: 你想除掉谁？

sentences.en: Oliver Cromwell, done.
sentences.zh: 奥利弗·克伦威尔，搞定。

sentences.en: Bang, gone.
sentences.zh: 砰，没了。

sentences.en: He's not even on trial.
sentences.zh: 他甚至都没有受审。

sentences.en: What are you talking about?
sentences.zh: 你在说什么？

sentences.en: You know...
sentences.zh: 你知道……

sentences.en: You dig him up.
sentences.zh: 你把他挖出来。

sentences.en: Dig him up.
sentences.zh: 把他挖出来。

sentences.en: This is shocking.
sentences.zh: 这太令人震惊了。

sentences.en: Stick his head on the bridge.
sentences.zh: 把他的头插在桥上。

sentences.en: On the bridge.
sentences.zh: 在桥上。

sentences.en: Saving, actually.
sentences.zh: 拯救，实际上。

sentences.en: I do think I know who I would save.
sentences.zh: 我确实知道我会拯救谁。

sentences.en: And in 1916, some men went into battle intending to die.
sentences.zh: 在1916年，有些人抱着必死的决心投入战斗。

sentences.en: The leaders, the signatories of the 1916 proclamation, they all expected to die should they lose.
sentences.zh: 领导人，1916年宣言的签署者，他们都预料到如果失败就会死。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But the president of the proclaimed republic, Patrick Pierce, his brother Willie was executed, tried and executed, and he probably shouldn't have been.
sentences.zh: 但宣布成立的共和国总统帕特里克·皮尔斯，他的弟弟威利被处决了，经过审判并被处决，他可能本不应该被处决。

sentences.en: So I would save Willie Pierce.
sentences.zh: 所以我想要拯救威利·皮尔斯。

sentences.en: Why would you say, why him and not the others?
sentences.zh: 你为什么会说，为什么是他而不是其他人？

sentences.en: Because he was...
sentences.zh: 因为他……

sentences.en: He's in the wrong place at the wrong time.
sentences.zh: 他在错误的时间出现在了错误的地点。

sentences.en: No, he was very junior.
sentences.zh: 不，他资历很浅。

sentences.en: He just had the wrong surname.
sentences.zh: 他只是姓错了。

sentences.en: You've only allowed him one.
sentences.zh: 你只允许他选一个。

sentences.en: I haven't.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: Well, I have only allowed him one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我只允许他选一个。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm so shocked by that Cromwell thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我对那个克伦威尔的事情感到非常震惊。

sentences.en: I can barely bring myself to...
sentences.zh: 我几乎无法让自己……

sentences.en: But I will do it because I'm a professional.
sentences.zh: 但我会做的，因为我是专业的。

sentences.en: I will tell people this is a brilliant exhibition.
sentences.zh: 我会告诉人们这是一个精彩的展览。

sentences.en: Neil, you've done a fantastic tour for us.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，你为我们做了一次精彩的导览。

sentences.en: The Cromwellian heresy aside.
sentences.zh: 撇开克伦威尔式的异端邪说不谈。

sentences.en: So, Tom, this is at the National Archives, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，这是在国家档案馆，对吧？

sentences.en: It's from the 5th of November.
sentences.zh: 这是11月5日的。

sentences.en: Yeah, what other date could it be?
sentences.zh: 是的，还能是什么日期？

sentences.en: 2022, obviously.
It's amazing to see all the documents.
sentences.zh: 看到所有的文件真是太棒了。

sentences.en: Tom, is it...
sentences.zh: 汤姆，是……

sentences.en: Does it cost any money to go to this exhibition?
sentences.zh: 参观这个展览需要花钱吗？

sentences.en: Do you know, Dominic, it costs zero pounds.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，多米尼克，它花费零英镑。

sentences.en: Do I need to book beforehand?
sentences.zh: 我需要提前预订吗？

sentences.en: You do not need to book.
sentences.zh: 你不需要预订。

sentences.en: Well, fantastic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，太棒了。

sentences.en: So, people...
sentences.zh: 所以，人们……

sentences.en: And Dominic, is there a book that goes for the exhibition?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，有没有关于这个展览的书？

sentences.en: Do you know, there's a website.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，有个网站。

sentences.en: There is a website, nationalarchives.gov.uk slash treason.
sentences.zh: 有个网站，nationalarchives.gov.uk 斜杠 treason。

sentences.en: But more excitingly, there is a book.
sentences.zh: 但更令人兴奋的是，还有本书。

sentences.en: Are you in this book, Neil?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，你在这本书里吗？

sentences.en: I wrote a book.
sentences.zh: 我写了一本书。

sentences.en: I co-wrote it.
sentences.zh: 我是合著者。

sentences.en: Oh, gee.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Are you talking about Cromwell in it?
sentences.zh: 你在书里提到克伦威尔了吗？

sentences.en: He gets a mention, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他有被提到，是的。

sentences.en: Dominic, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，多米尼克。

sentences.en: I read it, and it's absolutely fine.
sentences.zh: 我读过了，写得相当不错。

sentences.en: Does it?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: He behaves himself.
sentences.zh: 他表现得规规矩矩。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well, so, the book has the Tom Holland seal of approval, for what that's worth.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以这本书得到了汤姆·霍兰的认可，虽然这可能也没什么分量。

sentences.en: It's called History of Treason, the bloody history of Britain through the stories of its most notorious traitors.
sentences.zh: 书名叫《叛国史》，通过英国最臭名昭著的叛国者的故事，讲述了英国血腥的历史。

sentences.en: The exhibition, it's running till the end of the year, beyond?
sentences.zh: 展览会持续到年底吗，还是更久？

sentences.en: It runs until April.
sentences.zh: 会持续到四月。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Is there any excuse for people to miss it?
sentences.zh: 人们还有什么借口错过它吗？

sentences.en: I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 我想没有。

sentences.en: It's really good.
sentences.zh: 它真的很棒。

sentences.en: It shows off the sort of the breadth and the wealth and the depth of the collections here at the National Archives.
sentences.zh: 它展示了国家档案馆馆藏的广度、丰富性和深度。

sentences.en: So, do come along and see.
sentences.zh: 所以，一定要来看看。

sentences.en: We've done our best to interpret it for you and bring you on the journey of treason across the centuries from the 1352 Act onwards.
sentences.zh: 我们尽了最大努力为您解读，带您踏上从1352年《叛国法》开始，跨越几个世纪的叛国历史之旅。

sentences.en: Tom, it would be treason to miss it.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，错过它简直就是叛国。

sentences.en: Not to come.
sentences.zh: 不来就是。

sentences.en: It would be.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And on that bombshell.
sentences.zh: 以这个重磅消息结束。

sentences.en: Thank you, Neil.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，尼尔。

sentences.en: Thank you to the National Archives for having us, and thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢国家档案馆接待我们，也感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.zh: 想要获取加更剧集、抢先收听、无广告体验以及加入我们的聊天社区，请访问 restishistorypod.com 注册。
